name: epoll_pwait
synopsis: int epoll_pwait(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, int timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable sigmask);
description: epoll_pwait waits for events on an epoll file descriptor, similar to epoll_wait, but allows specifying a signal mask to handle signals atomically. It blocks until an event occurs, a signal is caught, or the timeout expires.

parameters.name: epfd
parameters.description: The epoll file descriptor to wait on

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of epoll_event structures to store the events

parameters.name: maxevents
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to be returned

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout value in milliseconds; -1 for indefinite blocking

parameters.name: sigmask
parameters.description: Pointer to a signal set to temporarily modify the signal mask

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors ready for I/O, or zero if no events occurred before timeout
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: epfd is not a valid file descriptor
The memory area pointed to by events is not accessible with write permissions
The call was interrupted by a signal handler
epfd is not an epoll file descriptor, or maxevents is less than or equal to zero

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.37, a timeout value larger than approximately LONG_MAX / HZ milliseconds is treated as -1 (i.e., infinity).
